div.head: CHAP. IV.
div.p: IN this Chapter, 1. The Lord confirms yet further, the difference to be betwixt the godly and the wicked, by ſhewing the judgements to come on the wicked, v.

q.p: For behold, the day cometh that ſhall burne as an Oven, and the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly ſhall be ſtubble, and the day that cometh ſhall burne them up, ſaith the LORD of hoſtes, that it ſhall leave them neither root nor branch.

div.p: The particle for ſhewes that the Lord is confirming that aſſertion, chap. 1.18. of a viſible difference to be betwixt the godly and the wicked. And firſt, for

q.p: But unto you that feare my Name, ſhall the Sun of righteouſneſſe ariſe with healing in his wings, and ye ſhall go forth and grow up as Calves of the ſtall.

div.p: As for the godly, he promiſes to ſend Chriſt unto them, bringing illumination, righteouſneſſe, healing, protection, and encreaſe of grace, and joy in the Holy

q.p: And ye ſhall tread down the wicked: for they ſhall be aſhes under the ſoles of your feete, in the day that I ſhall do this, ſaith the LORD of hoſtes.

div.p: To make this difference yet more conſpicuous, he not only threatens judgements againſt the wicked, and promiſes ſpiritual comforts to the godly, but promiſes

q.p: Remember the Law of Moſes my ſervant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Iſrael, with the ſtatutes and judgements.

div.p: This Prophecie, (as alſo the reſt, he being the laſt) is cloſed with ſome directions to the Church, whereof the firſt is, that ſince there was no other

q.p: Behold, I will ſend you Elijah the Prophet, before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD.

div.p: A ſecond direction is, earneſtly to expect Chriſts coming, and to prevent any miſtake about it, he premoniſhes them, that he would ſend John Baptiſt in the

q.p: And he ſhall turne the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, leſt I come and ſmite the earth with a curſe.
